name: Oregon
source: Oregon Department of Revenue withholding tax formulas 150-206-436 for 2026 (https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/withholding-tax-formulas_206-436_2026.pdf, read in validation run 3, 2026-10-22): 2026 brackets, standard deduction 2,910 / 5,820 and exemption credit 263; the 2025 Form OR-40 instructions and the 2025 quick reference sheet for the 65-or-older additions; second sources: taxbracketcalc.com and TaxAct Oregon guides (rates 4.75% to 9.9%)

state_base.note: Brackets: 2026 rates 4.75%, 6.75%, 8.75% and 9.9% from 0, 4,550 and 11,400 and 125,000 single (9,100, 22,800 and 250,000 joint), read on the DOR 2026 withholding tax formulas (https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/withholding-tax-formulas_206-436_2026.pdf, confirmed primary, validation run 3, 2026-10-22); their constants (678, 10,618, 1,357, 21,237) match the cumulative bases. The 125,000 / 250,000 top thresholds are not indexed; the lower ones are. Oregon starts from federal adjusted gross income, so 401(k) deferrals, deductible Traditional IRA deposits and HSA deposits stay deductible (not checked against DOR guidance). Not modelled: the subtraction of federal income tax paid (up to 8,750 for 2026, phased out from 125,000 to 145,000 single and 250,000 to 290,000 joint in 1,750 steps; 2026 withholding formulas, https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/withholding-tax-formulas_206-436_2026.pdf, validation run 3, 2026-10-22; law-backlog default 11), which overtaxes most returns by up to about 740; the 9% retirement income credit (income-limited); the kicker credit; and the exemption credit's end above a federal AGI of 100,000 single and 200,000 joint.

standard_deduction.note: 2026 Oregon standard deduction (DOR withholding tax formulas 150-206-436, https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/withholding-tax-formulas_206-436_2026.pdf, confirmed primary, validation run 3, 2026-10-22).

exemptions.note: The standard deduction rises by 1,000 for each married person 65 or older (1,200 for a single filer; the file uses 1,000 for both). Oregon's exemptions are credits (exemption_credits). The 65-or-older amounts are the 2025 ones (2026 not read).

exemption_credits.note: 2026 exemption credit 263 per person and per dependent (DOR withholding tax formulas 150-206-436, https://www.oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/withholding-tax-formulas_206-436_2026.pdf, confirmed primary, validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Not modelled: no credit above a federal AGI of 100,000 single and 200,000 joint.

estate_inheritance.check_at: ORS 118.010 and the Oregon DOR estate transfer tax page (https://www.oregon.gov/dor/programs/individuals/pages/estate.aspx)
estate_inheritance.note: Oregon estate tax (ORS 118.010): 10% of the Oregon taxable estate from 1,000,000 to 1,500,000, then 10.25%, 10.5%, 11%, 11.5%, 12%, 13%, 14%, 15% on each further 1,000,000 band, 16% above 9,500,000 (base 1,022,500 at 9,500,000). Rate table from the Legislative Revenue Office 2025 estate tax document (apps.oregonlegislature.gov, search extract); 1,000,000 exemption and no portability agree in Nolo and Mercer Advisors. SB 1511 (2026), which would have raised the threshold to 2,500,000 from 2027, died at adjournment (Lebanon Local News, secondary). No inheritance tax. Not modelled: the natural-resource credit.

social_security.note: Oregon subtracts all Social Security benefits included in federal AGI; it is not among the states that tax them in Kiplinger 2026 (https://www.kiplinger.com/taxes/states-that-tax-social-security-benefits) and AARP, as listed in .claude/state/research/state-costs.md. Confirmed primary on https://oregon.public.law/statutes/ors_316.054 (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

local_income_tax.note: The statewide transit tax withheld from every employee's wages: 0.1%. HB 3991 would have doubled it, but its referred parts (Measure 120) failed on 2026-05-19 and the Department of Revenue says to keep withholding at 0.1% (https://www.oregon.gov/dor/programs/businesses/Pages/statewide-transit-tax.aspx, validation run 2, 2026-10-22). Not modelled: the Portland Metro supportive housing services tax (1% of taxable income above 125,000 single / 200,000 joint) and the Multnomah County Preschool for All tax (1.5% above the same amounts, 3% above 250,000 / 400,000), which reach only high incomes in the Portland area, and the employer-paid TriMet and Lane transit payroll taxes.

sales_tax.check_at: Oregon revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://zamp.com/resources/sales-tax-on-groceries and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: assumed equal to the combined rate. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: no); research note: No sales tax. clothing_taxable is false (research: no; No sales tax). Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.check_at: Census ACS 2024 1-year tables B25090 and B25082 at https://data.census.gov
property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.note: Oregon two-year passenger registration 126 (0-19 mpg) or 136 (20-39 mpg), 63 to 68 a year, plus county fees (Multnomah 112, Washington and Clackamas 60 per two years), about 70 a year on average (unconfirmed county share). Oregon has no annual vehicle property tax; the HB 3991 increase was referred as Measure 120, which failed in May 2026. Typical car (29,100 list price, 2026 Toyota Camry LE), averaged over about ten years of ownership; registration and vehicle taxes only (no title, plate or inspection fees). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

fuel.source: Excise: https://www.oregon.gov/odot/FTG/Pages/Current%20Fuel%20Tax%20Rates.aspx (validation run 3, 2026-10-22); price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel; average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Gas excise confirmed primary: $0.40 per gallon, effective January 1, 2024 (no 2026 change listed) (validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 3, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Oregon insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Research note: ACA state age curve: age-60 value uses federal curve (approx). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
